retired.name: AlphaSync 2.0 for macOS 13 and later
retired.body:
# AlphaSync 2.0

AlphaSync is a free Mac app for reading, copying, and backing up files from an **AlphaSmart Neo** writing device. Connect your Neo with a USB cable to read your writing on your Mac, save a copy, or send text back to the Neo.

**Version 2.0, build 149, requires macOS 13 Ventura or later.** There are downloads for Intel and Apple Silicon Macs. For macOS 11 Big Sur or macOS 12 Monterey, use [AlphaSync 1.5.1](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/releases/tag/v1.5.1).

AlphaSync was originally written by tSoniq. Version 2.0 is the first public release of a complete Swift rewrite. The new version number marks that change from 1.5.1 and the earlier Objective-C and Objective-C++ versions. The main purpose stays the same: getting your writing safely between your Neo and your Mac.

## What it does

- **Read your Neo’s files.** Open a file in a separate, read-only window, search its text, and copy the complete text to the clipboard.
- **Copy files in either direction.** Save files through the File menu or by dragging them into Finder. Import text files, or drop one onto a file to replace its contents after confirmation.
- **Back up your writing.** Save the included files in dated folders, with a result that shows what finished and where it was saved.
- **Keep recovery copies.** Before replacing or clearing a file, save its original text and original Neo data. If a requested recovery copy fails, the change stops.
- **Open automatically.** Enable automatic opening in Settings to start AlphaSync when you connect a Neo.

## What is different from 1.5.1

The app has been rebuilt with Apple’s current Mac tools. It has a sidebar for choosing a Neo or one of its applets, a file table, native Settings, and separate windows for reading and file information. It follows your Mac’s Light or Dark appearance.

Recovery copies now include the original Neo data as well as readable text. File previews refresh after changes. Imports and exports keep their original targets while a file chooser is open, and interrupted exports explain which files were saved. Failed connections wait for Refresh or Try Again instead of repeatedly retrying in the background.

The minimum system has changed to macOS 13. Both downloads offer the same features. The Apple Silicon edition contains only the code needed for an M-series Mac and uses the newer icon; the Universal edition also includes Intel code and uses the original icon.

AlphaWord and user dictionary files can be imported and changed. Other applet files can be read, exported, and backed up as XML, but cannot be imported or changed by this version.

## How to download it

Check your macOS version and chip in **Apple menu → About This Mac**, then choose one download:

| Download | Which Mac? |
| --- | --- |
| [**Universal**](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/releases/download/v2.0/AlphaSync-2.0-149-macOS-13-universal.zip) | Intel or Apple Silicon, running macOS 13 or later. Choose this if you are unsure. |
| [**Apple Silicon**](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/releases/download/v2.0/AlphaSync-2.0-149-macOS-13-apple-silicon.zip) | An M-series Mac running macOS 13 or later. |

Install one edition. Each ZIP contains **AlphaSync.app** and its bundled automatic-launch helper. The separate **symbols** ZIPs are for developers investigating crashes.

## How to install it

1. Double-click the downloaded ZIP file to unpack it.
2. Quit an older copy of AlphaSync if it is running.
3. Drag **AlphaSync** into your **Applications** folder. Replace the older copy if Finder asks.
4. Open **Applications**, then double-click **AlphaSync**.

These downloads are not Apple-notarised. If macOS blocks the first opening, follow [Apple’s instructions for opening a downloaded app](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/102445). The approval is in **System Settings → Privacy & Security**. Use it only for the copy you downloaded from this release page.

If you used automatic opening in an older version, check it again in **AlphaSync → Settings…** after installing. Follow any Login Items approval prompt. Keep the app and its bundled helper together.

## How to use it

Open AlphaSync, then connect your Neo with a USB cable. Choose the Neo or applet in the sidebar. If a connection fails, review its message and choose **Try Again** or **Refresh**.

- **Read:** double-click a file. Choose Regular or Monospaced, use **Copy to Clipboard**, or search with **Edit → Find**.
- **Save to your Mac:** select files and choose **File → Save to Mac…**, or drag their names into a Finder folder. Existing Mac files are kept, and another copy gets a different name.
- **Add text to your Neo:** choose AlphaWord or the user dictionary, clear the file selection, then choose **File → Import Text Files to Neo…**.
- **Replace text:** select one file and import one text file, or drop a text file onto its name. Check the named target in the warning before continuing.
- **Back up:** click **Backup**. Choose the destination and optional backup log in **AlphaSync → Settings…**. An unfinished backup keeps **(Incomplete)** in its folder name.
- **Clear:** select files for **Clear File…** or **Clear Selected Files…**. With an applet selected and no files selected, **Clear All Files…** clears that applet’s files. **Cancel** is the default in every destructive warning.

**Save a recovery copy first** is enabled by default. In Settings, choose **Open Recovery Copies** to find the saved originals. Restore text by importing its saved `.txt` file onto the matching Neo file. Keep the accompanying `.neo` files for recovery or diagnosis; they are not text imports.

Recovery copies are kept for 30 days by default. Settings offers 7, 30, or 90 days, or no automatic expiry. Expired recognised copies move to Trash when a new copy is made. Keep a separate backup of important writing.

If a file is too large or contains a character your Neo cannot store, AlphaSync explains the problem and stops the import. Shorten or edit the text, then try again.

For the built-in guide, choose **Help → AlphaSync Help** or press **⌘?**.

---

## Technical information

### Rewrite and differences from 1.5.1

The shipping application, login helper, protocol engine, codecs, and file operations are Swift, with Swift 6 strict concurrency checking. SwiftUI provides the main interface. Small public AppKit adapters provide selectable read-only text, the native Find bar, Help, workspace operations, and orderly termination on macOS 13.

The rewrite was developed under version 1.6, which was not published. Version 2.0 is its first public release. The original BSD-style licence and tSoniq copyright notices remain. There are no third-party runtime libraries or separately installed USB drivers.

Both Xcode targets use the same Swift package. Universal contains x86_64 and arm64; Apple Silicon contains arm64 only. Both apps and their matching helpers have a 13.0 deployment target. The Silicon edition has a compile-time architecture guard, but no exclusive transfer features or unmeasured performance claims.

The shared modules are `AlphaSyncCore`, `AlphaSyncHardware`, and `AlphaSyncUI`. USB handles and mutable connection state stay on one serial executor. The main actor receives immutable `Sendable` snapshots. Connection generations prevent queued work from being redirected after reconnection.

The transport uses public IOUSBHost bulk APIs. Public HID output reports switch the Neo from its keyboard mode to its bulk-transfer mode. The helper reads attachment metadata only. It does not capture keyboard input, register a driver extension, or perform file transfers itself.

### File handling and fixes

- **Strict conversion:** exports and backups use UTF-8 without a byte-order mark, with LF line endings. Imports accept UTF-8, BOM-marked UTF-16 in either byte order, and MacASCII (Mac Roman). A declared UTF-8 file cannot silently fall back to Mac Roman after invalid bytes.
- **Validation before writing:** converted bytes must pass fresh applet limits and available-memory checks. Unsupported characters and names are rejected without replacement or truncation. Changed contents are read back for verification.
- **Recovery before changes:** requested copies preserve readable text, exact raw `.neo` bytes, and identification metadata before writing. A failed copy blocks the change. Recovery metadata is version 2; optional backup logs are version 3.
- **Original targets:** file chooser and drop requests capture their connection, applet, and file identities before asynchronous work. A lost original connection stops the request.
- **Current previews:** Inspector tasks include a content revision, so replacement, clearing, and explicit refresh invalidate cached text even when the file ID and allocation stay the same.
- **Structured failures:** device changes retain verified counts, possible unverified writes, underlying errors, and recovery locations. Export failures retain completed output URLs and the destination. Presentation does not infer outcomes by parsing English messages.
- **Controlled retries and cancellation:** failed connections and mode switches retain their errors until an explicit retry or detachment. Read-only work checks cancellation between blocks; an active write and its verification finish before shutdown. Transfer deadlines use `ContinuousClock`.
- **Local file protection:** exports use exclusive atomic publication and private permissions. Failed backups keep their incomplete marker. Drag exports advertise plain text or XML correctly. Staging keeps promised files available and removes recognised inactive sessions older than seven days, while locks protect active sessions.

### Differences from tSoniq’s latest release

[tSoniq’s latest published release is AlphaSync 1.3](https://github.com/tSoniq/alphasync/releases/tag/RELEASE_1_3). It already offered drag-and-drop transfers, backups, text conversion, and automatic opening. Version 2.0 keeps those core functions while replacing the earlier implementation, updating the native interface, adding current Mac architecture support, and carrying forward the file-protection work introduced in the 1.5 series.

### Install

The app embeds `Contents/Library/LoginItems/AlphaSyncLauncher.app`. Apps and helpers retain the identifiers `com.tsoniq.AlphaSync` and `com.tsoniq.AlphaSyncLauncher`, share version 2.0 and build 149, and use `SMAppService` for automatic opening on every supported system. Install one edition in Applications before enabling it. Disable a separately installed legacy helper before replacing an installation that uses one.

The release channel is `stable`, so About and Help link to the exact `v2.0` notes and licence. The preserved `v1.5.1` tag, `legacy-macos-11-12` branch, and their existing release assets remain separate.

The downloads have ad hoc code signatures, not Developer ID signatures or Apple notarisation tickets. Signature checks establish bundle integrity, not Apple approval or publisher identity. The build reports identify the signing state and exact source commit.

### Verification

Publication requires successful Intel and Apple Silicon build jobs, all 65 Swift regressions, packaging fixture checks, and native interface checks in Light and Dark appearances. Both native editions and their helpers are built and checked for exact architectures, macOS deployment targets, versions, bundle identifiers, selected icons, Help resources, hardened runtime, signatures, native dependencies, executable version output, and matching crash-symbol UUIDs.

The publication job downloads the resulting packages and checks all twelve assets again. It verifies SHA-256 hashes, source reports, archive contents, both extracted apps, and the extracted crash symbols before uploading a draft. Uploaded asset hashes must match before the draft becomes public. The build record linked below identifies the exact run.

Each app and symbols ZIP has a matching `.sha256` file and `.build-information.txt` report. Put the checksum beside its ZIP and run, for example:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c AlphaSync-2.0-149-macOS-13-universal.zip.sha256
```

The result should end in **OK**. After installation, check bundle integrity with:

```sh
codesign --verify --deep --strict /Applications/AlphaSync.app
```

Source-level checks and build instructions are in the [technical guide at v2.0](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/blob/v2.0/TECHNICAL.md).

**Testing limits:** hosted builds and simulations do not establish physical Neo compatibility. Physical Neo transfers, Login Items approval on actual installations, and runtime checks on macOS 13 remain unverified for this release. An earlier development build was reported working on macOS 27, but that report does not identify individual transfer or helper checks. The [manual checklist at v2.0](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/blob/v2.0/tests/manual-checks.md) records the outstanding work.

[Build and verification record](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/actions/runs/42714122125).

retired.name: AlphaSync 1.5
retired.body:
AlphaSync **1.5, build 146** improves file protection, transfer checks, and native Mac controls. Both downloads belong to this one testing release.

## Downloads

| Download | Mac |
|---|---|
| [For macOS 11 to macOS 26](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/releases/download/v1.5/AlphaSync-1.5-146-macOS-11-26-universal.zip) | Intel or Apple Silicon |
| [For macOS 27 and later](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/releases/download/v1.5/AlphaSync-1.5-146-macOS-27-apple-silicon.zip) | Apple Silicon only |

Choose one download for your Mac. Each contains **AlphaSync.app** and its automatic-launch helper. Checksums and build reports are separate downloads.

## What changed since 1.4.5

- **Recovery copies before replacing or clearing text.** This is on by default. AlphaSync saves the original text inside **Recovery Copies** in your backup folder before starting the change. If the requested copy cannot be completed, the change stops. Preferences offers 7-, 30-, and 90-day retention, or keeping copies until you remove them. The default is 30 days; expired recognised copies move to Trash when a new copy is made. **Open Recovery Copies** helps you find saved originals to restore manually.
- **Safer native confirmation sheets.** Replace and Clear warnings are attached to the main window. **Cancel** is the default, and the other button explicitly says **Replace**, **Clear File**, or **Clear All Files**.
- **Verification after changes.** Files are read back after writing or clearing. If AlphaSync cannot verify the result, it explains that contents may already have changed and gives the recovery location when a copy was saved.
- **Recognisable incomplete backups.** Dated folders keep **(Incomplete)** until that Neo’s backup succeeds, including when optional logs are off. Log paths continue to work when a completed folder loses its marker.
- **Clearer rename failures and natural sorting.** Unsupported or overlong names are rejected, unsuccessful renames are reported, and names such as File 1, File 2, and File 10 use Finder-style ordering.
- **Standard Edit and Find commands.** Copy, Select All, and Find work through the native Edit menu. Read-only file windows use the standard find bar and stay read-only. Preferences uses native scrolling when its form needs more space than the screen allows.
- **Bounded imports and fewer unnecessary reads.** Large local files are rejected without loading an unbounded amount of text. Full Neo file contents are read when needed for viewing, copying, or backup rather than for every list refresh.
- **Stricter USB replies and smaller release builds.** Unexpected response codes and malformed version fields are rejected. Interface test fixtures, unused resources, and debugging symbols are kept out of the app downloads. Matching crash symbols remain available as separate build artifacts. Documentation-only edits skip the full Mac build matrix.

Current guides and interface text use one space after a full stop. Exports and backups remain UTF-8, and imports accept MacASCII (Mac Roman), UTF-8, and UTF-16. Both editions use native Mac components and follow the system appearance.

## Install and open

Unpack the ZIP, move **AlphaSync** into **Applications**, and open it. Replace an older copy rather than installing both editions. If macOS blocks the first launch, follow the [installation and opening instructions](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/blob/v1.5/README.md).

## Testing

Automated checks cover simulated transfers, import limits and encodings, rename and verification failures, recovery scheduling, backup completion markers and logs, native sheets, read-only windows, menus, layouts, and appearance changes. Build checks cover both editions, app and helper versions, architectures, deployment targets, dependencies, signatures, archives, and matching separate crash symbols.

Real Neo transfers, recovery restoration and expiry, automatic-launch approval, and runtime behaviour on macOS 11 and 12 still need manual testing. Keep independent known-good backups while testing. This release remains a prerelease while those hardware and older-system checks are outstanding. See the [technical guide](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/blob/v1.5/TECHNICAL.md) and [manual checklist](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/blob/v1.5/tests/manual-checks.md).

retired.name: AlphaSync 1.4.5
retired.body:
AlphaSync **1.4.5, build 145** adds read-only file windows and a clearer Help menu, and improves the main window’s layout.  This is a testing release, with both Mac versions built from the same source.

## Downloads

| Download | Mac |
|---|---|
| [For macOS 11 to macOS 26](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/releases/download/v1.4.5/AlphaSync-1.4.5-145-macOS-11-26-universal.zip) | Intel or Apple Silicon |
| [For macOS 27 and later](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/releases/download/v1.4.5/AlphaSync-1.4.5-145-macOS-27-apple-silicon.zip) | Apple Silicon only |

Choose one download for your Mac.  Both contain **AlphaSync.app** and its automatic-launch helper.  Checksums and build reports are available as separate downloads.

## What changed since 1.4.4

- Double-click a file to open it in a separate, read-only window.  You can resize the window, scroll through the complete text, and select and copy it.  Reading a file leaves its contents on the Neo unchanged.
- Choose **Regular** or **Monospaced** in the file window’s **Font** control.  Both use the system font and default size.  New file windows remember your last choice.
- **Backup**, **Clear**, and **Info** now use matching native toolbar spacing.  The available-memory count stays at the right edge when you resize the main window, and long status messages fit alongside it.
- The Universal About panel now says **For macOS 11 to macOS 26**.
- The native **Help** menu groups the built-in guide, release notes for your installed version, the licence, and support links.  It uses the standard macOS Help search and **⌘?** shortcut.
- **AlphaSync on GitHub** opens the project.  **Report Issue…** opens a GitHub report with a simple template and the app and system details filled in.  **Contact Us…** opens an email to **mike@koralatov.com**.  You can edit either message before submitting or sending it.
- The licence is available offline in Help Viewer.  Help search is rebuilt from the current guide during each build, and the starting page now gives simple instructions for reading, copying, and backing up files.

The interface follows your Mac’s Light and Dark appearance automatically.  Exports and backups use UTF-8, and imports accept MacASCII (Mac Roman), UTF-8, and UTF-16.

## Install and open

Unpack the ZIP, move **AlphaSync** to **Applications**, and open it.  Replace an older copy rather than installing both versions together.  If macOS blocks the first launch, follow the [installation and opening instructions](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/blob/v1.4.5/README.md).

## Testing

Automated checks cover both compiled apps, read-only file windows and font choices, native toolbar and status layouts, Help menu commands and destinations, the bundled licence, and changes between Light and Dark Mode.  They also run the existing text conversion, import-limit, backup, background-task, and Clear-warning checks.  Both downloads use the pinned release compilers.

Real Neo transfers, automatic-launch approval, and runtime behaviour on macOS 11 and 12 still need manual testing, as do interactive Help Viewer search and browser and mail hand-offs.  Back up your Neo’s files before testing transfers or clearing files.  This release remains marked as a prerelease while those checks are outstanding.  The [technical guide](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/blob/v1.4.5/TECHNICAL.md) explains the checks in more detail.

AlphaSync **1.4.4, build 144** improves the Inspector, file-size displays, backups, and import checks.  This is a testing release, with both Mac versions built from the same source.

## Downloads

| Download | Mac |
|---|---|
| [For macOS version 11 to 26](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/releases/download/v1.4.4/AlphaSync-1.4.4-144-macOS-11-26-universal.zip) | Intel or Apple Silicon |

## What changed since 1.4.3

- The Inspector now has a Finder-style layout using native macOS controls.  **Preview** and **More Info** stay open, with clear headings, separators, and aligned labels.  Detail values can be selected and copied, and long text wraps to fit.
- File previews can be scrolled and copied.  Selecting several items or clearing the selection removes the previous item’s details.

The interface follows your Mac’s Light and Dark appearance automatically.  Exports and backups use UTF-8, and imports accept MacASCII (Mac Roman), UTF-8, and UTF-16.

## Install and open

Unpack the ZIP, move **AlphaSync** to **Applications**, and open it.  Replace an older copy rather than installing both versions together.  If macOS blocks the first launch, follow the [installation and opening instructions](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/blob/v1.4.4/README.md).

## Testing

Automated checks cover both compiled apps, text conversion, file-size and memory limits, rejected imports, backup logs, background tasks, native windows, Inspector layouts, Clear-warning defaults and response handling, and changes between Light and Dark Mode.  Both downloads use the pinned release compilers.

Real Neo transfers, automatic-launch approval, and runtime behaviour on macOS 11 and 12 still need manual testing.  Back up your Neo’s files before testing transfers or clearing files.  This release remains marked as a prerelease while those checks are outstanding.  The [technical guide](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/blob/v1.4.4/TECHNICAL.md) explains the checks in more detail.

retired.name: AlphaSync 1.4.1
retired.body:
This is a testing release of the modernised AlphaSync app, version **1.4.1, build 141**.

## Downloads

| Download | macOS | Mac |
|---|---|---|
| Universal | 11 through 26 | Intel or Apple Silicon |
| Modern | 27 and later | Apple Silicon |

Both downloads contain **AlphaSync.app** and its automatic-launch helper.  Choose the ZIP for your Mac.  The accompanying `.sha256` files let you check the downloads, and the build reports record their version and source revision.

## What changed

- Two Mac versions now come from the same source and share the same app version.
- Native Mac controls, system icons, and Help pages follow Light and Dark Mode, including changes while the app is running.
- Text exports and backups use UTF-8.  Imports still accept MacASCII (Mac Roman), UTF-8, and UTF-16.
- File transfers run in the background so the app stays responsive.  Disconnecting a NEO stops queued work from reaching a replacement connection.
- Safer file saving preserves existing exports, and backup reports distinguish completed, failed, cancelled, and interrupted backups.
- Preferences reports the automatic-launch state and provides access to the relevant Mac settings when approval is needed.
- The README now explains installation and everyday use in plain English, with a separate technical guide for advanced users.

## Install and open

Unpack the ZIP, move **AlphaSync** to **Applications**, and open it.  If macOS blocks the first launch, follow the [installation and opening instructions](https://github.com/koralatov/alphasync/blob/v1.4.1/README.md).  Replace an older copy rather than installing both versions together.

## Testing

The automated checks cover builds on Intel and Apple Silicon Macs, text conversion, file saving, backup reports, background tasks, and Light and Dark Mode.  The required release builds use the pinned compilers for macOS 26 and macOS 27.

Real NEO transfers, automatic-launch approval, and runtime behaviour on macOS 11 and 12 still need manual testing.  Back up your NEO’s files before testing transfers.  This release is marked as a prerelease while those checks remain outstanding.
